Exact_Title: DeepFace: Closing the Gap to Human-Level Performance in Face Verification
Authors: Yaniv Taigman, Ming Yang, Marc'Aurelio Ranzato, Lior Wolf
Venue: IEEE Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition (CVPR 2014)
Specific_Question_Addressed: Unconstrained face verification across severe out-of-plane pose, non-rigid expression, and lighting variation.
Proposed_Method: 3D facial landmark alignment (piecewise affine warping via 67 fiducials) coupled with deep 9-layer CNN with locally connected layers.
Dataset_and_Sample_Characteristics: Social Face Classification (SFC, 4.4M images, 4,030 identities), LFW, YTF.
Evaluation_Protocol: LFW 6,000 pair verification protocol (unrestricted, labeled outside data).
Metrics_and_Reported_Results: 97.35% accuracy on LFW, reducing error rate by 27% compared to previous non-deep baselines.
Generalization_Limitations: Locally connected layers lack weight sharing, scaling model parameters to 120M; requires explicit 3D mesh.
Dataset_or_Training_Data_License_Issues: Proprietary Meta/Facebook weights; closed commercial rights.
Relevance_to_Kelasagara: Demonstrates the necessity of strict 2D/3D affine canonical alignment prior to deep feature representation.
What_the_Evidence_Supports: 97.35% accuracy on LFW, reducing error rate by 27% compared to previous non-deep baselines.
What_the_Paper_Does_Not_Establish: Does not prove zero-error recognition under uncontrolled rural mobile environmental factors.

Exact_Title: Deep Learning Face Representation from Predicting 10,000 Classes
Authors: Yi Sun, Xiaogang Wang, Xiaoou Tang
Venue: IEEE Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition (CVPR 2014)
Specific_Question_Addressed: Extracting robust, compact identity features invariant to interpersonal identity changes.
Proposed_Method: Deep hidden identity representations (DeepID) trained via multiclass classification softmax over 10,000 identities across multiple facial crops.
Evaluation_Protocol: LFW standard 10-fold verification protocol.
Metrics_and_Reported_Results: Achieved 97.45% verification accuracy; shows multiclass classification creates strong linear separability.
Generalization_Limitations: Multi-region ensemble requires 60 separate CNN passes; impractical on mobile devices.
Relevance_to_Kelasagara: Underpins the principle that classification loss creates inter-class margin for downstream biometric comparison.
What_the_Evidence_Supports: Achieved 97.45% verification accuracy; shows multiclass classification creates strong linear separability.
What_the_Paper_Does_Not_Establish: Does not prove zero-error recognition under uncontrolled rural mobile environmental factors.

Exact_Title: Deep Learning Face Representation by Joint Identification-Verification
Authors: Yi Sun, Xiaogang Wang, Xiaoou Tang
Venue: Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems (NeurIPS 2014)
Specific_Question_Addressed: Balancing intra-class variance reduction with inter-class identity separation.
Proposed_Method: Joint identification (softmax cross-entropy) and verification (contrastive pairwise loss) multi-task learning.
Evaluation_Protocol: LFW standard 10-fold cross validation.
Metrics_and_Reported_Results: 99.15% accuracy on LFW; proved that identification loss enforces inter-class dispersion while contrastive loss contracts intra-class distances.
Generalization_Limitations: Contrastive loss requires careful mining of hard negative and positive pairs.
Relevance_to_Kelasagara: Directly guides Kelasagara's twin requirement: 1:1 verification requires intra-class contraction, while 1:N duplicate detection requires wide inter-class margin.
What_the_Evidence_Supports: 99.15% accuracy on LFW; proved that identification loss enforces inter-class dispersion while contrastive loss contracts intra-class distances.
What_the_Paper_Does_Not_Establish: Does not prove zero-error recognition under uncontrolled rural mobile environmental factors.

Exact_Title: FaceNet: A Unified Embedding for Face Recognition and Clustering
Authors: Florian Schroff, Dmitry Kalenichenko, James Philbin
Venue: IEEE Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition (CVPR 2015)
Specific_Question_Addressed: Intermediate bottleneck representations in classification networks require secondary metric calibration.
Proposed_Method: Direct mapping from face pixels to compact Euclidean space via triplet loss with semi-hard negative online mining.
Dataset_and_Sample_Characteristics: Google Private Dataset (100M-200M images, 8M identities), LFW, YouTube Faces.
Evaluation_Protocol: Squared L2 distance thresholding on 128-d unit hypersphere.
Metrics_and_Reported_Results: 99.63% accuracy on LFW, 95.12% on YouTube Faces. 128-d embedding suffices for state-of-the-art verification.
Generalization_Limitations: Semi-hard negative mining is cubic O(N^3), exceptionally unstable without massive batch sizes (>2000).
Relevance_to_Kelasagara: Demonstrates why unit hypersphere L2 normalization allows dot products to equal cosine similarity, simplifying mobile matching.
What_the_Evidence_Supports: 99.63% accuracy on LFW, 95.12% on YouTube Faces. 128-d embedding suffices for state-of-the-art verification.
What_the_Paper_Does_Not_Establish: Does not prove zero-error recognition under uncontrolled rural mobile environmental factors.

Exact_Title: A Discriminative Feature Learning Approach for Deep Face Recognition
Authors: Yandong Wen, Kaipeng Zhang, Zhifeng Li, Yu Qiao
Venue: European Conference on Computer Vision (ECCV 2016)
Specific_Question_Addressed: Standard softmax cross-entropy loss only penalizes misclassification without pulling identity features towards class centroids.
Proposed_Method: Center loss: simultaneously learns a center for deep features of each class and penalizes Euclidean distances between features and centers.
Evaluation_Protocol: Joint softmax + center loss minimization.
Metrics_and_Reported_Results: LFW 99.28%; dramatically shrinks intra-class variance in feature space.
Generalization_Limitations: Class center updates stored in GPU memory scale linearly with identity count, limiting scale beyond 100k identities.
Relevance_to_Kelasagara: Shows mathematical necessity of compact intra-class clustering to avoid drift in mobile edge capture.
What_the_Evidence_Supports: LFW 99.28%; dramatically shrinks intra-class variance in feature space.
What_the_Paper_Does_Not_Establish: Does not prove zero-error recognition under uncontrolled rural mobile environmental factors.

Exact_Title: L2-constrained Softmax Loss for Discriminative Face Verification
Authors: Rajeev Ranjan, Carlos D. Castillo, Rama Chellappa
Venue: arXiv preprint / IEEE SPL 2017
Specific_Question_Addressed: Unconstrained feature norms allow high-quality faces to have large norms while low-quality faces have tiny norms, distorting softmax gradients.
Proposed_Method: Constraining L2-norm of feature vectors to a fixed radius parameter alpha, forcing features to lie on a hypersphere.
Evaluation_Protocol: Fixed hypersphere radius scaling.
Metrics_and_Reported_Results: Stabilized training, boosting verification on poor quality images by preventing feature collapse.
Generalization_Limitations: Radius alpha is a sensitive hyperparameter requiring manual tuning.
Relevance_to_Kelasagara: Foundational rationale for why all Kelasagara embeddings are L2-normalized onto unit sphere S^(D-1).
What_the_Evidence_Supports: Stabilized training, boosting verification on poor quality images by preventing feature collapse.
What_the_Paper_Does_Not_Establish: Does not prove zero-error recognition under uncontrolled rural mobile environmental factors.

Exact_Title: SphereFace: Deep Hypersphere Embedding for Face Recognition
Authors: Weiyang Liu, Yandong Wen, Zhiding Yu, Ming Li, Bhiksha Raj, Le Song
Venue: IEEE Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition (CVPR 2017)
Specific_Question_Addressed: Euclidean margins are inherently inconsistent with angular metric nature of hyperspherical embeddings.
Proposed_Method: Angular Softmax (A-Softmax) loss: introduces multiplicative angular margin m * theta to force learned features onto a hyperspherical manifold.
Evaluation_Protocol: MegaFace 1M distractor challenge.
Metrics_and_Reported_Results: LFW 99.42%, MegaFace rank-1 identification 75.77% with small training set.
Generalization_Limitations: Multiplicative margin m leads to non-monotonic angular functions requiring piecewise surrogate functions and dynamic annealing.
Relevance_to_Kelasagara: Demonstrated that angular distance on a hypersphere is the natural metric for biometric identity discrimination.
What_the_Evidence_Supports: LFW 99.42%, MegaFace rank-1 identification 75.77% with small training set.
What_the_Paper_Does_Not_Establish: Does not prove zero-error recognition under uncontrolled rural mobile environmental factors.

Exact_Title: NormFace: L2 Hypersphere Embedding for Face Verification
Authors: Feng Wang, Xiang Xiang, Jian Cheng, Alan L. Yuille
Venue: ACM Multimedia (MM 2017)
Specific_Question_Addressed: Mismatch between training objective (inner product) and testing phase (cosine similarity).
Proposed_Method: Explicit normalization of both feature vectors and agent class weights to unit length during training with temperature scaling s.
Evaluation_Protocol: Cosine distance verification.
Metrics_and_Reported_Results: Normalization eliminates gradient bias towards frequent classes; verified optimal scaling parameter s.
Generalization_Limitations: Lacks margin between classes, leaving decision boundaries fragile near class edges.
Relevance_to_Kelasagara: Provides theoretical proof that unit feature normalization eliminates sample brightness and contrast artifacts.
What_the_Evidence_Supports: Normalization eliminates gradient bias towards frequent classes; verified optimal scaling parameter s.
What_the_Paper_Does_Not_Establish: Does not prove zero-error recognition under uncontrolled rural mobile environmental factors.

Exact_Title: Additive Margin Softmax for Face Verification
Authors: Feng Wang, Jian Cheng, Weiyang Liu, Haijun Liu
Venue: IEEE Signal Processing Letters (SPL 2018)
Specific_Question_Addressed: Multiplicative angular margins in SphereFace cause severe optimization instability.
Proposed_Method: Additive margin softmax: replaces cos(m*theta) with cos(theta) - m.
Evaluation_Protocol: MegaFace 1M challenge.
Metrics_and_Reported_Results: Converges effortlessly without annealing; outperforms SphereFace on MegaFace rank-1 (72.47%).
Generalization_Limitations: Margin m is fixed across all samples regardless of image quality.
Relevance_to_Kelasagara: Direct mathematical progenitor of CosFace and modern margin penalties.
What_the_Evidence_Supports: Converges effortlessly without annealing; outperforms SphereFace on MegaFace rank-1 (72.47%).
What_the_Paper_Does_Not_Establish: Does not prove zero-error recognition under uncontrolled rural mobile environmental factors.

Exact_Title: CosFace: Large Margin Cosine Loss for Deep Face Recognition
Authors: Hao Wang, Yitong Wang, Zheng Zhou, Xing Ji, Dihong Gong, Jingchao Zhou, Zhifeng Li, Wei Liu
Venue: IEEE Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition (CVPR 2018)
Specific_Question_Addressed: Maximizing inter-class variance while minimizing intra-class variance in cosine space.
Proposed_Method: Large Margin Cosine Loss (LMCL): L2 normalized features and weights with additive cosine margin m subtracted from target cosine score.
Evaluation_Protocol: Standard verification and 1:N MegaFace protocol.
Metrics_and_Reported_Results: LFW 99.73%, MegaFace 77.11% rank-1 with small training; simple, highly stable convergence.
Generalization_Limitations: Boundaries can compress in dense angular regions.
Relevance_to_Kelasagara: Demonstrates why cosine similarity is monotonic to identity separation.

Exact_Title: ArcFace: Additive Angular Margin Loss for Deep Face Recognition
Authors: Jiankang Deng, Jia Guo, Niannan Xue, Stefanos Zafeiriou
Venue: IEEE Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition (CVPR 2019)
Specific_Question_Addressed: CosFace cosine margin lacks direct geodesic geometric interpretability on the hypersphere.
Proposed_Method: Additive Angular Margin Loss: cos(theta + m) penalty in angular space, directly penalizing geodesic distance on unit hypersphere.
Dataset_and_Sample_Characteristics: MS1MV2, LFW, CFP-FP, AgeDB-30, IJB-B, IJB-C, MegaFace.
Evaluation_Protocol: Extensive 1:1 verification and 1:N identification across NIST/IJB benchmarks.
Metrics_and_Reported_Results: LFW 99.83%, IJB-C TAR@FAR=1e-4 95.6%, MegaFace 98.36% rank-1. Established the gold standard in deep face representation.
Generalization_Limitations: Angular margin m is uniform for all samples; low-quality or mislabeled samples generate excessively steep gradients.
Dataset_or_Training_Data_License_Issues: MIT code license; insightface model weights subject to non-commercial academic research restriction.
Relevance_to_Kelasagara: Architectural baseline for modern biometric feature extraction and geometric loss formulation.
What_the_Evidence_Supports: LFW 99.83%, IJB-C TAR@FAR=1e-4 95.6%, MegaFace 98.36% rank-1. Established the gold standard in deep face representation.

Exact_Title: Probabilistic Face Embeddings
Authors: Yichun Shi, Anil K. Jain
Venue: IEEE International Conference on Computer Vision (ICCV 2019)
Specific_Question_Addressed: Deterministic point embeddings cannot express confidence or uncertainty for degraded, blurry, or low-resolution faces.
Proposed_Method: Represents each face as a Gaussian distribution in embedding space with mean mu and diagonal variance sigma.
Dataset_and_Sample_Characteristics: CASIA-WebFace, MS-Celeb-1M, LFW, CFP, IJB-A, IJB-C.
Evaluation_Protocol: Mutual likelihood score matching under probabilistic density.
Metrics_and_Reported_Results: Significant accuracy boost on unconstrained datasets; variance magnitude inversely correlates with image quality.
Generalization_Limitations: Doubles storage requirements (storing both mean and variance) and increases matching complexity.
Relevance_to_Kelasagara: Demonstrates why sample quality must be evaluated prior to deterministic template storage.
What_the_Evidence_Supports: Significant accuracy boost on unconstrained datasets; variance magnitude inversely correlates with image quality.
What_the_Paper_Does_Not_Establish: Does not prove zero-error recognition under uncontrolled rural mobile environmental factors.

Authors: Yuge Huang, Yuhan Wang, Ying Tai, Xiaoming Liu, Pengcheng Shen, Shaoxin Li, Jilin Li, Feiyue Huang

Venue: European Conference on Computer Vision (ECCV 2020)

Exact_Title: MobileFaceNets: Efficient CNNs for Accurate Real-Time Face Verification on Mobile Devices
Authors: Sheng Chen, Yang Liu, Xiang Gao, Zhen Han
